To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel class of dual targeting IGF1R-EGFRAntibodies that show potent anti-cancer efficacy in vivo and that we have identified important antibody fusion protein related differences on ADcc activity and receptor down-modulation.
we have developed bispecific antibodies targeting IGF-IR and EGFR with potent anti-tumour activity in pre-clinical models.

(i) we successfully developed novel bispecific IgG1 dual-targeting IGF-1-EGFR antibodies; (ii) the bispecific IGF1R-EGF antibodies show a strong format dependent increase in receptor down-regulation and ADCC activity compared to the combination of the parental antibodies and (iii) they show potent in vivo tumor inhibition in xenograft models
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of bispecific antibodies with dual specificity against the epidermal growth-factor receptor (EGFR) and the insulin-like growth-factor receptor (IGF-IR) to overcome resistance to therapy and to improve efficacy in cancer.
the generation of novel bispecific IgG1 antibodies with dual specificity for the IGF-IR and the EGFR.
the development and evaluation of novel bispecific antibodies for the simultaneous targeting of IGF-IR and EGFR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we were able to generate a novel class of bispecific IGF1R/EGFR antibody constructs that are stable, productive and potent in vitro and in vivo and thus represent a promising therapeutic strategy to simultaneously block IGF1R and EGF signaling.
bispecific antibodies represent an attractive and promising therapeutic strategy to simultaneously block two key components deregulated in multiple cancer forms.
the bispecific IGF1R-EGFRAbs XGFR2/4 are promising candidates for the treatment of multiple cancers, especially in combination with EGFR-targeting therapies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the bispecific antibody format can be successfully used for the simultaneous targeting of two different growth factor receptors and that the design of the antibody fusion protein has a strong influence on ADCC activity as well as receptor downmodulation.

the development of a bispecific antibody with the ability to simultaneously bind and inhibit two receptors is feasible and that such a format can be used to overcome the limitations of a monospecific approach and to achieve enhanced efficacy.
we developed bispecific IGF1R-EGFr antibodies with potent tumor growth inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design and engineering of bispecific IgG1 antibodies is feasible and that they can be successfully applied in cancer therapy.
the bispecific IGF1R-EGFRAntibodies are a potent and effective combination therapy for the treatment of cancer.
we have successfully generated bispecific antibodies that are stable, productive and have the potential to be developed as a novel treatment for cancer.
